- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or shows recent volatility, model often overshoots early peaks; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid “overbought” overreaction.  
- When sentiment is mixed or trending downward, model often fails to mean-revert; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true prices.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly bullish (≥0.8).  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows early decline after peak, model often misses it; add 1–2% downward adjustment in 10–15 day window.
